description:
Measure spacing in a rendered interface. Returns an inline report with a clear problem and correction, plus a short text summary. Full measurements remain available in the report and structuredContent. Use after UI changes when a browser or DOM evaluator is available. A Shopify theme preview or a React Native web export counts: run the script in that page. A native app on an iOS simulator (SwiftUI, or React Native) is measured from its accessibility tree instead: run `axe describe-ui --udid <simulator id>` (AXe: `brew install cameroncooke/axe/axe`; point `DEVELOPER_DIR` at Xcode if it asks) on each screen and pass the printed JSON as nativeStates. That needs no capture script and no widths.

This is the runtime counterpart to get-review-rules. It automatically loads the live visual-design rubric, but it does not guess pixel values from a screenshot. Exact claims come from DOM geometry.

It measures geometry only. A score of 100 is not visual approval: it cannot judge hierarchy or whether the design works, so look at a screenshot before you call a screen done.

Workflow:
1. Call with no states to receive a read-only browser capture script in structuredContent.captureScript. Use detail: "full" if your client reads only text; it includes the script in text. That call measures nothing.
2. Evaluate that script in each rendered state you need to review: at minimum 1440, 1728 and 390 wide. Also capture named hover, focus, selected, and open states when they change a control's surface or layout.
3. Call again with the captured states and the project's spacing scale when known. The layout counts as measured only when this second call returns status `completed`; reading the snapshot yourself is not a measurement. The report and summary start with the highest-priority correction. Read structuredContent.findings or use detail: "full" for every returned finding, measurement, and fix. Structured evidence retains captured geometry and optional screenshots for report renderers.
4. At desktop widths it also checks five layout roles (sidebar width, page inset, section gap, column gap, card padding) against one density: the density argument, else the density the page's kit declares, else the closest measured mode. structuredContent.density names the mode, where it came from, and each role's measured and expected value.

The capture reads visible layout geometry, computed spacing, corner radii, surface styles, the number of line boxes each text block rendered, short accessible labels for interactive controls, the text of headings, the alt text of images, and the page title. It does not collect source code, cookies, form values, or network data. Add data-bd-inspect-label, data-bd-symmetry, data-bd-group, data-bd-compare-size, data-bd-align-group, and data-bd-align-edge attributes when the intended relationship cannot be inferred safely.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used only for usage analytics; does not change the result.

density.description: The layout density to check against: compact, comfortable or spacious. Omit it to use the project's design config, then the design system's default, both read from the page's --layout-density variable, then the mode closest to the measured page.

detail.description: Defaults to a short summary alongside the inline report. Use full for the capture script or all findings and measurements in text-only clients.

nativeStates.description: Native screens: a name for each, and the JSON `axe describe-ui` printed for it. Frames are in points and are measured as pixels.

spacingScale.description: Project spacing tokens in CSS pixels. Defaults to 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128.

states.description: Rendered layout states from the capture script. Omit on the first call to receive the script.

density.description: The density the page declares through the kit's --layout-density variable. The capture script fills it.

label.description: The text a person sees on it: a button's or heading's text, or an image's alt text. Reports name the element by it.

screenshotDataUrl.description: Optional browser screenshot as a data URL. It remains in the structured evidence for report renderers and is not persisted.

title.description: The page title, document.title. The Review tab names the check by it.

tolerance.description: Pixel tolerance for grouping measurements. Defaults to 1px.

name: inspect-spacing
